label: Utilization of the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment Data for Advanced Modeling and Simulation of Smoke Generation in Micro-Gravity
title: Utilization of the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment Data for Advanced Modeling and Simulation of Smoke Generation in Micro-Gravity
tier_reason: Team list, Tier 2. Ground study; PSI subarea: Smoke Aerosol, Combustion Simulation.

summary_student.text: This was a computer study, not a flight experiment: it simulated the smoke given off when a heated material releases vapor, both with gravity and without it. Without gravity, hot gas does not rise and mix in the same way, so the smoke particles grow differently. Understanding this difference helps build better smoke detectors and prevent fires.

summary_professional.text: Ground-based direct numerical simulation (Navier-Stokes nodal approach) of the formation and growth of dibutyl-phthalate (DBP) smoke particles from pyrolysis vapor expelled by a heated sample, in a geometry similar to the SAME experiments, under Earth gravity and microgravity. Two low cross-flow velocities were considered, slow enough that buoyancy matters in gravity. The study assessed how particle size distributions depend on thermophoresis, particle settling and flow geometry, and used instantaneous scalar fields to describe particle accumulation and growth in buoyant and non-buoyant wakes downstream of the hot vapor source.

pillar.reason: The record states that models of smoke particles would directly lead to better smoke detection devices; the study simulates smoke from a geometry similar to the SAME smoke experiments.
